headline: A small studio for
buildings that *don't*
exist yet.
paragraphs: Studio Morfis was founded in {founded}. In {experience} years we have handled local and international projects, from small private houses to large infrastructure, for architects, engineers, developers and public clients.
We make still images, films and interactive walkthroughs. The tools change; the questions stay the same: where the light comes from, how a material feels, and how a place will be used.

principles.title: Start from the drawings
principles.body: Every image is built from the architect's own plans, sections and models. We do not invent what has not been designed.

principles.title: Light before detail
principles.body: We set the sun, the sky and the hour before placing a single object. Most of an image is decided by its light.

principles.title: One image, one idea
principles.body: Each view should say one thing about the building. A few precise images serve a project better than many.

principles.title: Honest materials
principles.body: Concrete, timber and stone keep their real grain, weathering and imperfection, so a design can be judged as it will be built.

projects.title: The Monolithic Void
projects.team: A. Morfis, M. Sørensen, J. Pires
projects.lead: Stills and a short film for a concrete house above the Atlantic, built around a single cut of light.
narrative: The architects needed images of an idea most clients find hard to picture: a house made almost entirely of one material, with a single opening on its entrance façade.
We modelled the board-formed concrete from the shuttering drawings, plank by plank, and spent most of the commission on one question: where the nine-metre slot of light falls at each hour of the day.
The final set is eight stills and a ninety-second film that follows the blade of light from the hall to the dining table, from morning to dusk.

figures.caption: Entrance hall, the nine-metre light slot
The house from the lower terrace

projects.title: Timber Pavilion
projects.team: A. Morfis, L. Kragh, T. Ono
projects.lead: Interior stills and a walkthrough film for a sixty-metre gallery of spruce fins beside a fjord.
narrative: The pavilion is a single long room whose character comes from rhythm: two hundred and forty fins that open and close as you walk along it.
Still images could not show that, so the centrepiece of the commission is a slow walkthrough film, timed to a visitor's pace, with the fjord light shifting through the fins.
Six stills accompany the film. They were used in the planning application and later in the foundation's fundraising campaign.

projects.title: House of Clay
projects.lead: A series of quiet interior images for a rammed-earth house on the Alentejo plain.
narrative: Rammed earth is hard to render convincingly. Its layers, colour shifts and soft edges give away any shortcut.
We photographed test walls on site with the builder and built the material from those references, so the images show the walls the house will actually have.
The commission ended with five stills at different hours, from the cool blue of early morning to the warm light of late afternoon.

figures.caption: Living room, morning light on clay

projects.title: Basalt Archive
projects.team: A. Morfis, M. Sørensen, E. Gunnarsdóttir
projects.lead: Competition and design-stage images for a public archive wrapped in a screen of basalt fins.
narrative: The archive began as a competition entry. Our first image was made in nine days and helped the design team win.
Since then we have followed the design through each stage, updating the façade study as the fins changed depth and spacing to suit the low northern sun.
The final film and street-level stills are in production for the building's opening in 2027.

projects.title: Chapel of Still Light
projects.lead: Two images and a year-long light study for a small stone chapel lit only from above.
narrative: The brief was modest: one exterior and one interior image for the parish's fundraising leaflet.

The interior became a study of its own. We tested the roof glazing in every month of the year to show how light would slide down the dry-laid stone, and the architects used the results to adjust the width of the glass band.

figures.caption: Light falling along the north wall

projects.title: Courtyard Houses
projects.team: A. Morfis, L. Kragh, C. Ferrer
projects.lead: Aerial and courtyard views for eighteen social homes arranged around walled gardens.
narrative: Housing images are often bright, busy and generic. The brief asked for the opposite: calm views that show what daily life in a shaded courtyard would feel like.
We produced one aerial of the whole carpet of courtyards and a set of eye-level views, each planted with the single tree its future residents will inherit.
